brief.situation: 16:10 in a family practice. You are the nurse practitioner. Ms. Ortiz, 34, flew back from Manila four days ago. Her left calf has ached since, and this afternoon she felt short of breath climbing the stairs to the office.
handover: Takes a combined oral contraceptive. No past clots. The medical assistant has drawn a D-dimer tube 'to save time' and asks whether to send it to the outside lab (results tomorrow).
Practice policy: suspected pulmonary embolism with a high pretest probability, or any hypoxia, chest pain or syncope, goes to the emergency department the same visit; the hospital is 10 minutes away.
The practice has a pulse oximeter, an ECG machine and oxygen.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each assessment takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings are telling you.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Ms. Ortiz is now hypoxic with pleuritic pain. What does her probability mean for testing, and what do you do?

parts.label: What it means
parts.criteria: A swollen tender calf after a long flight on estrogen, tachycardia, then pleuritic pain and hypoxia: high pretest probability of PE; a D-dimer won't change management at high probability, CT pulmonary angiography will.
parts.modelAnswer: Her Wells score is high: DVT signs, tachycardia, long travel, estrogen, and now pleuritic pain and hypoxia. At high probability a D-dimer won't change what we do; she needs CT pulmonary angiography.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Emergency department now by ambulance; oxygen and stay with her; don't send the D-dimer and wait; hand off.
parts.modelAnswer: Ambulance to the emergency department now for CT angiography, oxygen and stay with her, and no waiting on a D-dimer.

scoring.modelReasoning: Calf swelling after a long flight on a combined pill with a fast heart rate gives a high Wells score before any test. At high pretest probability a D-dimer won't change management, so it isn't the test to order; CT pulmonary angiography is. When she becomes hypoxic with pleuritic pain, she goes to the emergency department now by ambulance.

ddQ.ask: While you examine her: when is a D-dimer the right first test for suspected PE?
ddQ.explain: Intermediate probability: a high-sensitivity D-dimer as the initial test; high probability: CT pulmonary angiography, and no D-dimer.
